chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The perfume in the moustache is from the character of the Prophets (peace be upon them) and a prestige for the Scribes.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of applying perfume to the moustache in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the aesthetic practice of applying perfume to the moustache with the noble character (*akhlaq*) of the Prophets, elevating it from mere grooming to a spiritual attribute. This act is further described as a mark of honor (*karamah*) for the recording angels (*al-Katibin*), suggesting that such beautification pleases the divine record-keepers and reflects inner purity. This tradition underscores the Shia emphasis on *Zinah* (beautification) as an act of worship when done with the right intention, aligning physical appearance with spiritual dignity.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Shuayb, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The perfume in the moustache is from the mannerism of the Prophets<sup>as</sup> and a prestige for the two Scribes (recording Angels)’.
en.sarwar: 15. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman from Shu’ayb from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Applying perfume is of moral discipline of the Prophets and honoring the scribes (the two angels on one’s shoulders).”’
